root_idea.summary: The supplied lexical record centers on moisture: earth becomes moist, is moistened, and retains moisture; ثَرًى names moisture or moist earth and can also denote the earth or soil.
root_idea.development: The physical notion of moist ground develops into inchoative, causative, and participial forms, as well as figurative extensions involving freshness, accessible benefit, and unbroken connection.

qac_form_accounting.reason: The sole QAC group is an independently attested Quranic noun; its inflected Quranic surface is normalized to the classical citation form ثَرًى.

senses.definition: Earth or soil, especially the ground beneath which something lies.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic expression مَا تَحْتَ الثَّرَى, it denotes what is beneath the earth or soil.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become moist and soft after drought or dryness.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of earth or land, including land watered by rain that penetrates to its moisture.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To moisten, sprinkle, or pour water over and mix into something.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of a place, earth, ground, dust, food preparations, and similar substances, including sawiq and aqit.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make the hands cling to the ground between the two prostrations of prayer.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional description of keeping the hands pressed to the ground until the second prostration.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To moisten the earth; to become abundant or compact with moisture.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The verb may describe rain moistening the earth or land becoming richly moist.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Moisture or humidity of the earth; moist earth, and also the earth or soil.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The expression مَثْرِيٌّ is used as an intensive epithet for very moist earth.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The earth's moisture, especially in the conventional expression describing its meeting with rainwater.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: In اِلْتَقَى الثَّرَيَانِ, the two moistures meet when rain has sunk into the ground and reached the earth's own moisture.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The pubic hair and the soft hair of a fur garment.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is an idiomatic use based on the comparison with moist earth and fur.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Moisture-producing rain at the beginning of the rainy season.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: In شَهْرٌ ثَرَى, it refers to a month in which rain begins, sinks into the ground, and moistens and softens the earth.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Moisture identified as a horse's sweat as it appears.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: In بَدَا ثَرَى المَاءِ مِنَ الفَرَسِ, the expression refers to the appearance of the horse's sweat.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The visible effect of anger in a person's face.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative use in إِنِّي لَأَرَى ثَرَى الغَضَبِ فِي وَجْهِ فُلَانٍ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Good or benefit that is readily obtainable.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: In قَرِيبُ الثَّرَى, it describes someone from whom good seems easy to attain, by comparison with moisture near the surface of the earth.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A promise that appears near to fulfillment but is not fulfilled.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: In قَرِيبُ الثَّرَى بَعِيدُ النَّبَطِ, it characterizes a person who promises but does not fulfill.
In لَمْ يَبْبَسِ الثَّرَى بَيْنِي وَبَيْنَهُ, the moisture of the earth metaphorically represents friendship that has not withered or been severed.
Used adjectivally of land, a place, or a day; it may describe earth made moist and soft by rain.
Used of land whose earth has not become dry; it is the active participial form associated with أَثْرَى.

cautions: No Maqāyīs or Mufradāt evidence was supplied, so the root-level orientation is limited to the directly attested lexical field.
The Quranic form has one QAC occurrence, in the expression مَا تَحْتَ الثَّرَى at 20:6:12. Historical lexical citation notation is not treated as an additional modern verse location.
The broader moisture, derived-verb, adjectival, anatomical, and figurative branches are Classical Arabic meanings and are not additional Quranic occurrences.
